title: Multi-valued Topological Groups: Vietoris Continuity, Complete Parts, and Fundamental Quotients
content: We develop a topological framework for group-like algebraic systems whose multiplication is genuinely multi-valued. The central object is a hyperoperation ◦ : G × G −→ P∗(G), where P∗(G) denotes the family of all nonempty subsets of G. We focus on the compactvalued case ◦ : G × G −→ K(G), where K(G) is the hyperspace of all nonempty compact subsets of G, and impose continuity with respect to the full Vietoris topology. This provides a natural refinement of the usual upper hyperspace approach to topological hyperstructures. We formulate the notion of a Vietoris multi-valued topological group using the axioms of a polygroup, rather than using weaker identity and inverse conditions. This choice guarantees a strong algebraic connection with ordinary groups and permits the construction of fundamental quotients. We establish basic properties of continuous multi-valued translations, inversion, division, compact products, closed graphs, products, subgroups, and continuous homomorphisms. A central role is played by complete parts. We introduce Vietoris-complete multi-valued topological groups, prove that complete open neighborhoods generate natural left and right neighborhood systems, and construct canonical left and right uniform structures. We then investigate the fundamental relation and prove that, under a natural complete-part hypothesis, the fundamental quotient carries a canonical topological group structure. We also establish a singleton-collapse theorem showing that the proposed theory contains ordinary topological groups as a rigid special case. Several examples are developed, including finite hypergroups, quotient constructions, compact orbit hyperstructures, and finite-valued operations. The paper concludes with a comparison with Marty hypergroups, polygroups, and locally compact convolution hypergroups, together with open problems concerning completion, invariant measures, Lie-type structures, bitopological extensions, and multi-valued groupoids.
